Step 1 · Predict

This button calls setCount(count + 1) twice on every click. It starts at 0. What number does it show after 3 clicks?

Counter.jsx
  1. import { useState } from 'react';
  3. export default function Counter() {
  4. const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  6. function handleClick() {
  7. setCount(count + 1);
  8. setCount(count + 1);
  9. }
  11. return (
  12. <div>
  13. <p>{count}</p>
  14. <button onClick={handleClick}>Add</button>
  15. </div>
  16. );
  17. }
Correct. In one click, both calls read the same count, so both ask for the same number. It adds 1 per click.
Incorrect. Both calls read the count of that render. Both ask for count + 1, not count + 2.
Incorrect. setCount does change the state, and React re-renders. The question is how much each click adds.

With setCount((c) => c + 1) twice, it would reach 6.

Step 2 · Run in Cursor

Your task

Create a component with a button that shows and hides a message.

  1. In Cursor, open your React project built with Vite and run npm run dev.
  2. Create src/ShowHideMessage.jsx with a boolean state that starts as true (message visible).
  3. Add it to App.jsx.
  4. Click 3 times and look at the message.

Step 3 · Compare

Start with the message visible. After 3 clicks, can you see the message? Type yes or no.

Correct. 3 clicks flip the boolean 3 times, so it ends up hidden.
Not a match. Check your initial state: if it starts as true, 3 clicks leave it as false.
Type yes or no.

Step 3 · Compare

One possible solution

src/ShowHideMessage.jsx
  1. import { useState } from 'react';
  3. export default function ShowHideMessage() {
  4. const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(true);
  6. return (
  7. <div>
  8. <h1>Show and hide</h1>
  9. <button onClick={() => setIsVisible(!isVisible)}>
  10. {isVisible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}
  11. </button>
  12. {isVisible && <p>This is a message.</p>}
  13. </div>
  14. );
  15. }
Your version can be different and still be right: what matters is a boolean state, ! to flip it and && to render the message.

Step 3 · Compare

In short

  • Changing state re-renders. Changing a plain variable does not.
  • Each render has its own value. Two setCount(count + 1) calls in the same click read the same count.
  • A boolean and ! are enough to show and hide.
